pending_commit.commit_message: FROMGIT: rpmsg: Allow RPMSG_VIRTIO to be enabled via menuconfig or defconfig Currently, RPMSG_VIRTIO can only be enabled if some other kconfig option selects it. This does not allow it to be enabled for virtualized systems where Virtio RPMSG is available over Virtio MMIO or PCI transport. This patch updates RPMSG_VIRTIO kconfig option so that we can enable the VirtIO RPMSG driver via menuconfig or defconfig. The patch also removes "select RPMSG_VIRTIO" from various remoteproc kconfig options because it is now user selectable. Signed-off-by: Anup Patel <anup@brainfault.org> Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> (cherry picked from commit 4d91d7b099508831e82ef209bba71c8b636886a2 https://github.com/andersson/remoteproc rproc-next) BUG=none TEST=cheza modem Change-Id: I27ee21badd41de1e7dcc8ec4a60a8de01b0a7d54 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1271460 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: remoteproc: Remove depends on HAS_DMA in case of platform dependency Remove dependencies on HAS_DMA where a Kconfig symbol depends on another symbol that implies HAS_DMA, and, optionally, on "|| COMPILE_TEST". In most cases this other symbol is an architecture or platform specific symbol, or PCI. Generic symbols and drivers without platform dependencies keep their dependencies on HAS_DMA, to prevent compiling subsystems or drivers that cannot work anyway. This simplifies the dependencies, and allows to improve compile-testing. Signed-off-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert@linux-m68k.org> Reviewed-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> Acked-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com> Acked-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> (cherry picked from commit 41a5985f173bf1f93d2634fc93d8aa53683067f9 https://github.com/andersson/remoteproc rproc-next) BUG=none TEST=cheza modem Change-Id: I29ade6f31632783688970c5f55429c5917913f47 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1271461 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: qcom: sdm845-cheza: Add qspi nodes for SPI flash This enables / configures the SPI flash controller on sdm845-cheza. NOTES: * 104 MHz is specified in the datasheet of w25q128fw as the max speed of the flash chip. ...in theory the Quad SPI controller is supposed to support up to 80 MHz. ...but for now we'll use 25 MHz since higher speeds weren't reliable. * We can use 2 lanes to talk to the SPI since both the controller and the w25q128fw support it. Data / Chip Select should be always driven though so no need for a pull. cros-kernel2: Add a 'debug' use flag for general purpose debug features The kernel has many debug facilities that aren't turned on unless a specific use flag is specified when building the kernel. Let's add a generic 'debug' use flag that turns on all the debugging options so that developers can easily turn on all the various kernel config options for debugging. The assumption is that this use flag can and will degrade performance significantly. We want to use this to catch kernel bugs in test configurations, so this shouldn't be enabled in any sort of production systems. BUG=None TEST=Build and boot kernel, modprobe configs && check /proc/config.gz for all options enabled here modulo ones which are arch specific Change-Id: Idc76931a9113003b3d57312e183f445dc7c9eec8 Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1262158 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: drm/i915: Apply correct ddi translation table for AML device Amber Lake used the same gen graphics as Kaby Lake. Kernel driver should configure KBL's DDI buffer setting for AML ULX as well. chaps: Block shutdown while TokenInitThread runs Block powerd from emitting a shutdown signal while the TokenInitThread is running (~1-2secs) to prevent an unclean chapsd shutdown. Powerd shutdown signal is postponed by creating a lock file with chapsd's PID in /run/lock/power_override/. This lock file will be removed again once TokenInitThread finishes. BUG=chromium:892539 TEST=manual: Put some cert into system-wide slot, restart chapsd, close lid (=shutdown) while TokenInitThread is active (~1-2s). Logs should verify TokenInitThread completion (contain "Master key is ready for token ..." & "Postponing shutdown for lockfile(s): /run/lock/power_override/chapsd_token_init_slot_0.lock"). Additional Thread.sleep() in TokenInitThread might help with manual testing since it only runs for ~1-2s. CHROMIUM: config: Enable softlockup detector on all platforms This config is already enabled on x86 platforms, but it isn't enabled on arm64 or arm platforms. Enable it in the common config so that we can detect softlockups on the all architectures and make the system panic if this happens too. This matches how the v4.4 kernel works. This is this script: cat << EOF | tee -a chromeos/config/arm64/common.config chromeos/config/armel/common.config CONFIG_BOOTPARAM_SOFTLOCKUP_PANIC=y CONFIG_BOOTPARAM_SOFTLOCKUP_PANIC_VALUE=1 CONFIG_SOFTLOCKUP_DETECTOR=y EOF ./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig olddefconfig on top of a normalized config. BUG=None TEST=Build and boot kernel, modprobe configs && check for softlockup config enabled here Change-Id: I05451110d965c4b84f83d307920881087d632d7c Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1264256 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

arc-setup: Do not abort when arcbootcontinue command failed As mentioned in the code comment, the command fails when it is executed after the container is shut down (or in the middle of its shutdown or crash.) The command can fail, for example, if the Chrome browser process crashes right after sign in, or if Chrome browser restarts the container under severe OOM conditions. Since the command failure is not something we can directly fix, uploading arc-setup crash reports to the crash server is not something actionable. It only confuses people looking at crash/. This CL stops sending such reports, and instead just leave logs in /var/log/arc.log.
